attribution_limitations: MCTD certainty differs across the article: the abstract says the patient was ultimately diagnosed with MCTD-associated NSIP after confirmatory serologies, whereas the body says the serologies support a possible MCTD diagnosis and the MMF indication is suspected MCTD-associated NSIP. Biopsy-consistent NSIP is kept as a diagnosis; MCTD is kept as possible; the combined confirmed claim is review-only. Do not infer a confirmed MCTD diagnosis.
Potassium 5.0 mEq/L is flagged High although the printed reference range is 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; value and printed flag are kept as given without correcting either.
The authors state anti-CCP is negative, and the table flags 16 units as Normal with negative range below 20 units; the observation uses the negative interpretation with the numeric value 16 units.

Timing of the bronchoscopy, inflammatory-marker testing, serologies, echocardiography, paresthesia report and follow-up CT scans relative to one another and to the ICU transfer, steroids and discharge is mostly not stated; only explicitly worded orderings are linked. The reference point of the one- and six-month follow-up scans is not stated.

Authors suggest etiologies for anemia, hyponatremia, transaminitis, proteinuria, T3 and tachycardia (nutritional, alcohol, endocrine, inflammation, anxiety); these are hypotheses, not diagnoses, and are not recorded as patient conditions. The authors also state RF positive with negative anti-CCP may reflect the MCTD spectrum rather than classic RA; the earlier possible RA diagnosis remains unconfirmed.

Statements that NSIP often mimics infectious pneumonia and that patients may fail to improve despite antibiotics are generalizations; the article does not explicitly state that this patient failed to respond to cefepime/doxycycline before ICU transfer beyond worsening hypoxemia the next morning.

Routes are stated only for the initial intravenous methylprednisolone 60 mg regimen and the oral MMF 500 mg starting dose; the 500 mg daily methylprednisolone and MMF 1,000 mg twice-daily entries leave route unset rather than borrowing it from the neighbouring clause.
